content: 1. Krysiak R and Okopień B (2012) discussed common and less common causes of certain medical conditions in their publication in Polski Merkuriusz Lekarski. 2. Tanaka H (2005) explored clinical aspects of calcium metabolism in the journal Clinical Calcium. 3. Boente M del C, Asial RA, and Winik BC (2006) reported on a new family case of Geroderma osteodysplastica in Pediatric Dermatology. 4. Hennekam RC (2006) provided a comprehensive review of the phenotype associated with Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome in American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A. 5. Nojiri H et al. (2011) demonstrated that cytoplasmic superoxide contributes to bone fragility by inducing low-turnover osteoporosis and impairing collagen cross-linking, as published in Journal of Bone and Mineral Research. 6. Lekva T et al. (2012) identified that TXNIP is highly regulated in bone biopsies from patients with endogenous Cushing's syndrome and is related to bone turnover, as detailed in European Journal of Endocrinology. 7. Ferlin A, Schipilliti M, and Foresta C (2011) investigated bone density and the risk of osteoporosis in individuals with Klinefelter syndrome, as published in Acta Paediatrica. 8. Grasswick LJ and Bradford JM (2003) reviewed osteoporosis associated with the treatment of paraphilias, based on seven clinical case reports, in Journal of Forensic Sciences. 9. Vasireddy S and Swinson DR (2001) reported on male osteoporosis linked to long-term cyproterone treatment in Journal of Rheumatology. 10. Gold DT and Solimeo S (2006) examined the historical relationship between osteoporosis and depression in Current Osteoporosis Reports. 11. Dytfeld J and Horst-Sikorska W (2012) presented a case report on pregnancy-associated osteoporosis in Ginekologia Polska. 12. Elshal MF et al. (2012) investigated the association between bone mineral density, parathyroid hormone, and serum magnesium levels in adult patients with sickle-cell anemia, as published in Archives of Medical Science.
